items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: I remember when Frances Sweeney, who is prominent in the book, died, the only way I could get some kind of consolation was to play Ben Webster ballads again and again and again.

ctx.x: You talk about your mother really questioning almost your sanity about your choice of what you were pursuing.

She couldn’t understand it. She said it all sounds the same, this jazz. And I remember when Frances Sweeney, who is prominent in the book, died, the only way I could get some kind of consolation was to play Ben Webster ballads again and again and again. And I almost drove my mother crazy.
Do you think she’d be proud of what your accomplishments have been?
